Facts: Deceased's nephews (children of predeceased siblings) challenged authenticity of holographic will appointing cousin sole heir, claiming will not entirely written by deceased based on private graphological opinion establishing heterography; defendants countered with court-appointed expert confirming authenticity despite block-letter text versus cursive comparison writings.
Legal Framework: Articles 602, 606 Italian Civil Code (holographic will formalities); Art. 217(2) CPC (comparison document admissibility); established case law on holographic will challenges (Cass. SU 12307/2015, Cass. 5629/2020).
Interpretive Issues: Burden of proof allocation for negative-assessment action challenging holographic will authenticity; admissibility criteria for comparison documents when parties disagree on origin; evidentiary weight of private technical opinion versus court-appointed expert; whether structural differences between block-letter will and cursive comparison writings prevent authenticity finding; discretionary nature of technical investigation renewal requests.
Principles Applied: Party contesting holographic authenticity bears proof burden regardless of procedural position; raises quaestio inexistentiae removing succession title through falsity recognition. Holographic will possesses intrinsic demonstrative force differentiating it from ordinary private documents. Negative assessment action governed by general contract-challenge principles; no obligation for challenged party declaring intention to avail themselves of deed, either as independent requirement or by analogy with private-deed verification/disavowal principles. Comparison document admissibility per Art. 217(2) requires origin recognized or ascertained by court ruling/public deed absent party agreement. Documents whose deceased-origin unrecognized/unascertained excluded from comparison despite plaintiff production. Court-appointed expert using six handwritten signatures from 2012 notarial deed viewed in original form, qualitatively/quantitatively suitable reconstructing graphomotor path. Analytical-comparative graphoscopic analysis using instrumental techniques (digital microscope stroke analysis, Wood's lamp alteration verification) established authenticity ruling out forgery. Comparison identified distinctive characteristics/graphic heritage; emphasized clear consistency/compatibility elements especially unique unrepeatable personal marks and consistent graphic features; highest technical confidence expressed. Block-letter versus cursive difference overcome through analytical examination showing shared intrinsic handwriting characteristics in dynamic interaction (rhythmic frequency repetition, systematic connotation/marking combination) and impressive personalized-marking range unquestionably leading to handwriting-uniqueness judgment. Apparent structural differences fall within deceased's graphic variability. Trial judge not required ordering new expert opinion even upon explicit party request; renewal falls within discretionary powers; express ruling unnecessary. Court adheres to expert conclusions recognizing authenticity given rigorous assessment method and conclusion consistency. Date graphic layout not contemporary with text/signature; labored strokes attributable to more advanced graphomotor-aging stage.
